correctness.rationale: The discriminant identity 12(b^3-a^3)-3=(6t-3)^2 reduces the finite obstruction search to bounded integer pairs. Exact arithmetic finds 579 floor-admissible first-pair solutions through t=333333 and no triple-cube solution, with an independent direct-search cross-check through t=10000. The final range then follows from Applegate--Pratt Theorems 3.1 and 3.2 plus Corollary 3.5 and explicit residual bounds.

originality.rationale: Applegate--Pratt arXiv:2609.20505v1 states the triple-cube obstruction as an open conjecture and proves the prime-plus-two-cubes result only below 10^16. Exact and synonymous searches, the current source repository, and searches for the new endpoint found no matching stronger bound or the same finite reduction. Unindexed contemporaneous work remains a residual risk because the source preprint is very recent.

value.rationale: The verified prime-plus-two-positive-cubes boundary is increased from 10^16 to 333334^3=37037259259703704, while the specific triple-cube obstruction relevant to the bootstrap is exhausted through t=333333 by a compact reusable exact computation.
